BASIS OF PRESENTATION Organization Hallador Energy Company (“Hallador” or the “Company”) is a vertically-integrated, independent power producer (“IPP”) and fuel company with operations primarily in Indiana. The Company operates across multiple stages of the energy supply chain, from accredited capacity and electricity to coal. The Company’s condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Hallador and our wholly owned subsidiaries, including our main operating subsidiaries, Hallador Power Company, LLC (“Hallador Power”) and Sunrise Coal, LLC (“Sunrise”) and their respective subsidiaries, as well Turtle Creek Gas Holdings, LLC and its subsidiary Turtle Creek Gas Generation, LLC and Hourglass Sands, LLC. Additionally, we hold 50 % interests in Sunrise Energy, LLC (“Sunrise Energy”), a private gas exploration company with operations in Indiana and Oaktown Gas, LLC (“Oaktown Gas”), which we account for using the equity method. Hallador Power provides accredited capacity and energy to utilities and other energy market participants through the Midcontinent Independent System Operator ("MISO") interconnection, and Sunrise mines bituminous coal in Indiana to serve various power plants in the Midwest and Southeast United States. (5) DEBT KLIM Facility On September 15, 2026 (the “KLIM Closing Date”), the Company and its wholly owned subsidiary, Turtle Creek Gas Holdings, LLC (“Turtle Creek”), each as a co-borrower, jointly and severally liable for all obligations thereunder (and 6 Table of Contents together, the "KLIM Borrowers"), entered into a Credit Agreement (the “KLIM Credit Agreement”) with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as administrative agent, U.S. Bank National Association, as collateral agent, Kennedy Lewis Investment Management LLC ("KLIM"), acting for certain managed or advised funds and accounts, and the other lenders from time to time party thereto. The KLIM Credit Agreement provides for a senior secured term loan facility (the “KLIM Facility”) to finance the development and construction of a 460 MW natural gas-fired peaking generation facility in Sullivan County, Indiana (the “Turtle Creek Project”) to be owned and operated by Turtle Creek Gas Generation, LLC (“Turtle Creek Gas”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Turtle Creek. The KLIM Facility provides for term loans in an aggregate principal amount of up to $ 600.0 million, consisting of a $ 550.0 million initial term loan, which was funded in September 2026, and a $ 50.0 million delayed draw term loan commitment, which is available until September 15, 2027, subject to an agreed draw schedule and funding conditions. The delayed draw term loan may only be used to fund the Turtle Creek Project. As of September 30, 2026, no amounts had been drawn under the delayed draw term loan commitment. Amounts repaid or prepaid under the KLIM Facility may not be re-borrowed. The KLIM Facility matures on September 15, 2029, and may be extended for two additional years with the consent of the lenders upon payment of an extension fee equal to 3.0 % of the then-outstanding principal amount. The KLIM Credit Agreement also permits the Company to obtain, on a post-closing basis, a separate revolving credit facility of up to $ 75.0 million from one or more commercial banks. Any such revolving facility would not be documented under the KLIM Credit Agreement, but would be secured by a first-priority lien on the Company’s collateral, senior to the lien securing the KLIM Facility, and would be subject to an inter-creditor agreement between the lenders. As of September 30, 2026, no such revolving credit facility had been established. Turtle Creek Gas and certain other subsidiaries of the Company, including Hallador Power and Sunrise Coal, guarantee the obligations under the KLIM Facility. The obligations are secured by a first-priority perfected security interest in substantially all real and personal property of the Company, Turtle Creek and the subsidiary guarantors, including the equity interests of their subsidiaries (other than subsidiaries designated as unrestricted subsidiaries under the KLIM Credit Agreement), the Turtle Creek Project, the Merom Station, and certain mining assets of Sunrise Coal, subject to customary exceptions and, upon establishment of the revolving credit facility described above, an inter-creditor agreement. Prior to the date the Turtle Creek Project achieves commercial operation (the “Commercial Operation Date”), borrowings bear interest at (i) a fixed rate of 3.5 % per annum, payable in cash, plus (ii) Term SOFR plus 4.5 % per annum, which is paid-in-kind ("PIK") by adding such interest to the outstanding principal balance. On and after the Commercial Operation Date, borrowings bear interest at Term SOFR plus 8.0 % per annum, payable in cash. Term SOFR is subject to a floor of 3.5 %. As of September 30, 2026, the interest rate on borrowings under the KLIM Facility was 11.9 %, and the effective interest rate, including the amortization of debt issuance costs, was 14.7 %. On the KLIM Closing Date, Turtle Creek made an intercompany loan of $ 19.7 million to the Company to fund cash collateral for the Company’s outstanding letters of credit (the “Closing Date Intercompany Loan”). Under the KLIM Credit Agreement, the PIK interest rate on the KLIM Facility increases by 1.0 % per annum if the Closing Date Intercompany Loan remains outstanding after October 31, 2026, and by an aggregate of 3.0 % per annum if it remains outstanding after January 15, 2027, in each case until the loan is repaid in full. The Closing Date Intercompany Loan was not repaid by October 31, 2026, and as a result, effective November 1, 2026, the PIK interest rate on the KLIM Facility increased by 1.00 % per annum. As of the date of this Quarterly Report, the loan remains outstanding. The Company is required to pay its excess cash flow for fiscal year 2026 and each fiscal year thereafter (calculated excluding Turtle Creek and its subsidiaries and including the net proceeds of equity issuances and permitted convertible indebtedness) into the construction account to repay the Closing Date Intercompany Loan until it is repaid in full. Coal operations Our coal revenue is derived from sales to customers of coal produced at our mining facilities. We categorize each of our fair value measurements in one of these three levels based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety. These levels are: Level 1: Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities. Level 2: Quoted prices in markets that are not active, or inputs that are observable, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability. Level 3: Measured based on prices or valuation models that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and less observable from objective sources (i.e., supported by little or no market activity). The Company operates across multiple stages of the energy supply chain, from accredited capacity and energy to coal. The Company’s electric operations are located within the MISO footprint. Our operations include Hallador Power Company, LLC ("Hallador Power"), which provides accredited capacity and energy to utilities and other energy market participants through its MISO interconnection, and Sunrise Coal, LLC ("Sunrise"), which mines bituminous coal in Indiana to serve various power plants in the Midwest and Southeast United States. Operations Our business is organized based on the services and products we provide in two segments: (i) Electric Operations and (ii) Coal Operations. The Company also holds 50% interests in Sunrise Energy, LLC (“Sunrise Energy”) and Oaktown Gas, LLC (“Oaktown Gas”), which are accounted for using the equity method. Through its operating subsidiaries, the Company delivers three main products to its customers. Accredited Capacity. Hallador Power, the Company’s wholly owned electric subsidiary, owns and operates the Merom Station, a 1,080 MW coal-fired power generating station, consisting of two steam turbine generators. Unit 1 entered commercial operations in 1982 and Unit 2 in 1983. The units are dispatched through its MISO interconnection. In order to purchase energy through the MISO system, an end user must supply or purchase accredited capacity for an equivalent load. As accredited capacity is primarily available in large quantities from dispatchable sources of energy, such as natural gas and coal-fired power plants, Hallador Power sells accredited capacity to utilities and other energy market participants within the MISO system through Power Purchase Agreements (“PPA”) and other bilateral transactions. Energy. In addition to accredited capacity, Hallador Power sells wholesale energy to utilities, generation and transmission cooperatives, and other energy market participants within the MISO system through PPAs and other bilateral transactions, and sells on a spot basis in the day-ahead and real-time MISO markets. Coal. Sunrise, the Company’s wholly owned mining subsidiary, mines coal from reserves found in the Illinois Basin (“ILB”). Coal mined by Sunrise is used as a primary fuel source for generating electricity at various power plants in the Midwest and Southeast United States. In addition, Sunrise has a developed infrastructure for the transport of coal, which is typically sold free on board from the shipping point, including rail networks and truck loading systems, facilitating the efficient movement of the resource from the mine to its customers. Sunrise’s Oaktown Mining Complex is about twenty miles from Merom, enabling Merom and Sunrise to take advantage of low-cost fuel on a delivered basis. Strategy and Management Focus We view our business as two integrated operations, “Electric Operations” (our gigawatt Merom power generating station), and “Coal Operations” (our coal mining and coal sales group). We strive to achieve margin expansion through organic revenue growth and profitability in our operations by negotiating and fulfilling contracts for accredited capacity, wholesale energy, and thermal coal to utilities and other energy market participants. We continue to progress the development of the Turtle Creek Project, while monitoring opportunities to expand the capacity of our electric generation capabilities through further development, or via acquisition. We continue to evaluate other strategic transactions that could add diversification, durability, scale, and geographic expansion opportunities to our Electric Operations.
